words.definition: done carefully and completely, with attention to every detail.
examples: She did a thorough review of the migration plan before approving it.
We need a more thorough explanation — this one skips the hard parts.

words.definition: to use something you already have in order to get a better result.
examples: Let's leverage the existing cache instead of querying the database again.
The team leveraged their experience with the old system to move faster.

words.definition: the one slow part of a process that limits how fast the whole thing can go.
examples: Code review has become the bottleneck in our release process.
Profiling showed the bottleneck was disk access, not the network.

words.definition: to make a process simpler and more efficient by removing unnecessary steps.
examples: We streamlined onboarding from five forms down to one.
The goal is to streamline the workflow, not to add more tools.

words.definition: possible to do, with the time and resources you actually have.
examples: Shipping by Friday is feasible if we drop the export feature.
It sounds nice, but it is not technically feasible this quarter.

words.definition: a difference between two things that should be the same.
examples: There is a discrepancy between the invoice total and our records.
Can you explain the discrepancy in the two reports?
collocations: a discrepancy between X and Y

words.definition: to make something bad less severe, without removing it completely.
examples: We added a retry to mitigate the impact of network failures.
Nothing removes the risk entirely, but we can mitigate it.

words.definition: not needed, because the same thing already exists somewhere else.
examples: This check is redundant — the database already enforces it.
Two teams were doing redundant work for months.

words.definition: the limits of what a piece of work includes — and what it leaves out.
examples: Authentication is out of scope for this release.
The scope keeps growing, so the deadline keeps moving.

words.definition: a temporary way to avoid a problem instead of fixing its cause.
examples: Clearing the cache is a workaround, not a real fix.
We shipped a workaround so users are not blocked until Monday.

words.definition: to mark something as old and discouraged, before removing it later.
examples: We will deprecate the v1 endpoint in June and delete it in December.
That option is deprecated — use the config file instead.

words.definition: strong enough to keep working correctly when conditions get bad.
examples: The parser is robust: it survives malformed input without crashing.
We need a robust process that works even when people are on holiday.

words.definition: a situation where you accept losing one good thing to gain another.
examples: There is a trade-off between speed and memory usage here.
Every architecture is a trade-off; pick the one that fits your needs.
collocations: a trade-off between X and Y

words.definition: to make something easier to understand by explaining it more clearly.
examples: Could you clarify what you mean by "soon"?
Let me clarify one point before we vote on it.

words.definition: work that has piled up and is still waiting to be done.
examples: That idea is in the backlog, but nobody is working on it yet.
We spent a week clearing the backlog of support tickets.

words.definition: to pass a problem to someone more senior, or to make it grow worse.
examples: If the client does not reply by Thursday, escalate it to the manager.
A small disagreement escalated into a two-week argument.

words.definition: made of small, separate details rather than one big block.
examples: We need more granular permissions — read-only is too broad.
The report is too granular; give me the summary first.

words.definition: something that stops you from making any progress until it is solved.
examples: The missing API key is a blocker for the whole team.
Any blockers before we start the sprint?

words.definition: slow and awkward to use, because it is too heavy or complicated.
examples: The approval process is cumbersome: four signatures for one invoice.
This library is powerful but cumbersome for small scripts.

words.definition: a clear, useful understanding of why something happens.
examples: The logs gave us a real insight into how users actually navigate.
Thanks for that insight — it changes how I see the problem.
